## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

content.text: Confirmed. Here's the bug: **The landing page (`/`) never redirects anywhere after login, and it doesn't check auth state at all.** - Your "Sign in" / "Get started" buttons both just link to `/auth/login` with no `returnTo` param (`src/app/page.tsx:16,28`). - The Auth0 SDK (`@auth0/nextjs-auth0` v4) processes `/auth/login` → Auth0 Universal Login → `/auth/callback` via the middleware in `src/proxy.ts`, and when no `returnTo` was specified, it lands you back on `/` by default. - `src/app/page.tsx` is a plain static landing page — it never calls `auth0.getSession()`, so it renders identically whether you're logged in or not. You end up back on `http://localhost:3000/` looking at the exact same "Sign in" button, which looks like sign-in silently did nothing. - The actual authenticated app lives under the `(app)` route group (`/today`, `/pantry`, etc.), guarded by `src/app/(app)/layout.tsx`, which does call `requireUser()` — but nothing sends you there after login. So it's not failing — you *are* signed in, you're just stranded on a landing page that doesn't know or care that you're signed in. **Fix:** point the sign-in links at `/today` as the return destination, e.g.: ```tsx Get started ``` (`@auth0/nextjs-auth0` v4's `/auth/login` route accepts a `returnTo` query param.) Optionally, also make `page.tsx` check `auth0.getSession()` and show a "Go to app" link / redirect when already signed in, so a signed-in user hitting `/` isn't stuck looking at the marketing page either. content.text:
Yes — `now.were.cooking`, not `were.cooking`. Reasoning from the actual `Caddyfile`:

- The `were.cooking` block only serves `/`, `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico` directly (the `@landing` matcher). Everything else — including `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` — falls through to its `handle {}` block, which does `redir https://now.were.cooking{uri}`. So any auth request that hits `were.cooking` gets 302'd straight to `now.were.cooking` before it ever reaches the Next.js app.
- The `now.were.cooking` block only redirects the exact path `/` (either to `were.cooking` if logged out, or to `/today` if logged in); `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` don't match either `redir`, so they pass straight through via `import app` to the Next.js container.

So the OAuth round-trip always actually completes on `now.were.cooking`. That means:
- `APP_BASE_URL=https://now.were.cooking` — this is what `@auth0/nextjs-auth0` uses to build the `redirect_uri` it sends to Auth0.
- Auth0 dashboard **Allowed Callback URLs** must include `https://now.were.cooking/auth/callback` to match.
- `were.cooking` only needs to appear in **Allowed Logout URLs** (since logout can send you back to the marketing page) and doesn't need to be in Web Origins, since it never makes a direct auth request — it just issues an HTTP redirect at the edge.

So the earlier checklist was right as written — `now.were.cooking` for `APP_BASE_URL` and Web Origins, both domains for Logout URLs.

content.text:
Good news on the technical question: **no, you don't need real Auth0 access at all** for local dev, regardless of who holds the tenant credentials. Look at `src/lib/auth0.ts:9`:

```ts
export const authDisabled = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' && !process.env.AUTH0_DOMAIN;
```

If `AUTH0_DOMAIN` isn't set locally, the app auto-logs you in as a fake "Demo cook" user (`current-user.ts`'s `DEV_USER`) and skips Auth0 entirely — `src/proxy.ts` even short-circuits the middleware when this is on. So you can hit `/today`, `/recipes`, `/pantry`, anything behind login, without your friend's Auth0 dashboard access. (Your real `.env` currently has `AUTH0_DOMAIN` set, so you'd need to comment it out locally to flip this on — just don't commit that.)

One thing worth flagging though: I pulled up this repo's own team-assignment docs (`hang.md`, `johnny.md`, `jerry.md`) to check, and "what happens after login" — `/today` and `/onboarding` — are explicitly **Johnny's** owned files (Workstream B), while your area (Workstream C) is `src/features/recipes/**`, `src/app/(app)/recipes/**`, `src/app/api/{recipes,cook}/**`. The team rule in those docs is "only edit files you own, ask in chat before touching anyone else's." So technically you can build/test those pages, but if you mean actually implementing their content, that'd be worth a heads-up to Johnny first rather than me just diving in.

So: what specifically did you want to move on to — your own recipes/cook work, or did you want help on the `/today`/`/onboarding` stubs themselves?

content.text:
# Schedule Cloud Agents

You are helping the user schedule, update, list, or run **cloud** Claude Code agents. These are NOT local cron jobs — each routine spawns a fully isolated cloud session (CCR) in Anthropic's cloud infrastructure, either on a recurring cron schedule or once at a specific time. The agent runs in a sandboxed environment with its own git checkout, tools, and optional MCP connections.

## First Step

The user has already told you what they want (see User Request at the bottom). Skip the initial question and go directly to the matching workflow.

## Setup Notes

⚠ Heads-up:
- Not in a git repo — you'll need to specify a repo URL manually (or skip repos entirely).


## What You Can Do

Use the `RemoteTrigger` tool (load it first with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger`; auth is handled in-process — do not use curl):

- `{action: "list"}` — list all routines
- `{action: "get", trigger_id: "..."}` — fetch one routine
- `{action: "create", body: {...}}` — create a routine
- `{action: "update", trigger_id: "...", body: {...}}` — partial update
- `{action: "run", trigger_id: "..."}` — run a routine now

(Note: the API uses `trigger_id` as the parameter name, but the user-facing term is "routine".)

You CANNOT delete routines. If the user asks to delete, direct them to: https://claude.ai/code/routines

## Create body shape

For a recurring schedule:

```json
{
  "name": "AGENT_NAME",
  "cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR",
  "enabled": true,
  "job_config": {
    "ccr": {
      "environment_id": "ENVIRONMENT_ID",
      "session_context": {
        "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
        "sources": [
          {"git_repository": {"url": "https://github.com/ORG/REPO"}}
        ],
        "allowed_tools": ["Bash", "Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep"]
      },
      "events": [
        {"data": {
          "uuid": "<lowercase v4 uuid>",
          "session_id": "",
          "type": "user",
          "parent_tool_use_id": null,
          "message": {"content": "PROMPT_HERE", "role": "user"}
        }}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

For a one-time run, replace `"cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR"` with `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"` (RFC3339 UTC, must be in the future). Everything else is identical.

Generate a fresh lowercase UUID for `events[].data.uuid` yourself.

## Available MCP Connectors

These are the user's currently connected claude.ai MCP connectors:

Connected connectors (available for routines):
- claude.ai Claude Docs (connector_uuid: 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c, name: Claude-Docs, url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/pages/mcp)

When attaching connectors to a routine, use the `connector_uuid` and `name` shown above (the name is already sanitized to only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores), and the connector's URL. The `name` field in `mcp_connections` must only contain `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` — dots and spaces are NOT allowed.

**Important:** Infer what services the agent needs from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack connectors. Cross-reference against the list above and warn if any required service isn't connected. If a needed connector is missing, direct the user to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect it first.

## Environments

Every routine requires an `environment_id` in the job config. This determines where the cloud agent runs. Ask the user which environment to use.

Available environments:
- Default (id: env_016iXpGnPz5ciHrGSipKaWby, kind: anthropic_cloud)

Use the `id` value as the `environment_id` in `job_config.ccr.environment_id`.


## API Field Reference

### Create Routine — Required Fields
- `name` (string) — A descriptive name
- Exactly ONE of:
  - `cron_expression` (string) — 5-field cron in UTC. **Minimum interval is 1 hour.**
  - `run_once_at` (string) — RFC3339 UTC timestamp. Must be in the future. Fires once, then auto-disables.
- `job_config` (object) — Session configuration (see structure above)

### Create Routine — Optional Fields
- `enabled` (boolean, default: true)
- `mcp_connections` (array) — MCP servers to attach:
  ```json
  [{"connector_uuid": "uuid", "name": "server-name", "url": "https://..."}]
  ```

### Update Routine — Optional Fields
All fields optional (partial update):
- `name`, `cron_expression`, `run_once_at`, `enabled`, `job_config`
- `mcp_connections` — Replace MCP connections
- `clear_mcp_connections` (boolean) — Remove all MCP connections

### Cron Expression Examples

The user's local timezone is **America/Vancouver**. Cron expressions and `run_once_at` timestamps are always in UTC. When the user says a local time, convert it to UTC but confirm with them: "9am America/Vancouver = Xam UTC, so the cron would be `0 X * * 1-5`." For one-time runs, the same conversion applies — "run this at 3pm" → `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z"` with their 3pm converted to UTC.

- `0 9 * * 1-5` — Every weekday at 9am **UTC**
- `0 */2 * * *` — Every 2 hours
- `0 0 * * *` — Daily at midnight **UTC**
- `30 14 * * 1` — Every Monday at 2:30pm **UTC**
- `0 8 1 * *` — First of every month at 8am **UTC**

Minimum interval is 1 hour. `*/30 * * * *` will be rejected.

### Current Time (for one-off runs)

When /schedule was invoked it was **Sun, Nov 8, 2026 at 03:49 AM** (America/Vancouver) / **2026-11-08T10:49:27.132Z** UTC. Treat this as an approximate anchor only — the conversation may have been running for a while since then.

**Before computing any `run_once_at` value, you MUST re-check the current time** by running `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` via the Bash tool. Do not guess or infer today's date from conversation context. Resolve relative requests ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 3 hours", "next Monday") against the freshly fetched time, then echo the resolved local time AND the UTC timestamp back to the user for confirmation before creating the routine. If the resolved time is already in the past, ask the user to clarify rather than silently rolling forward.

## Workflow

### CREATE a new routine:

1. **Understand the goal** — Ask what they want the cloud agent to do. What repo(s)? What task? Remind them that the agent runs in the cloud — it won't have access to their local machine, local files, or local environment variables.
2. **Craft the prompt** — Help them write an effective agent prompt. Good prompts are:
   - Specific about what to do and what success looks like
   - Clear about which files/areas to focus on
   - Explicit about what actions to take (open PRs, commit, just analyze, etc.)
3. **Set the schedule** — Ask when and how often. The user's timezone is America/Vancouver. When they say a time (e.g., "every morning at 9am"), assume they mean their local time and convert to UTC for the cron expression. Always confirm the conversion: "9am America/Vancouver = Xam UTC." If they want a one-time run (e.g., "once at 3pm", "tomorrow morning", "remind me to check X later"), use `run_once_at` instead of `cron_expression` — same timezone conversion applies. **First re-check the current time with `date -u` via Bash** (the reference time above may be stale in a long conversation), resolve the relative phrase against that fresh value, and confirm the resulting absolute timestamp with the user.
4. **Choose the model** — Default to `claude-sonnet-5`. Tell the user which model you're defaulting to and ask if they want a different one.
5. **Validate connections** — Infer what services the agent will need from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack MCP connectors. Cross-reference with the connectors list above. If any are missing, warn the user and link them to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect first. Ask which git repos the cloud agent needs cloned into its environment.
6. **Review and confirm** — Show the full configuration before creating. Let them adjust.
7. **Create it** — Call `RemoteTrigger` with `action: "create"` and show the result. The response includes the routine ID. Always output a link at the end: `https://claude.ai/code/routines/{ROUTINE_ID}`

### UPDATE a routine:

1. List routines first so they can pick one
2. Ask what they want to change
3. Show current vs proposed value
4. Confirm and update

### LIST routines:

1. Fetch and display in a readable format
2. Show: name, schedule (human-readable), enabled/disabled, next run, repo(s)

### RUN NOW:

1. List routines if they haven't specified which one
2. Confirm which routine
3. Execute and confirm

## Important Notes

- These are CLOUD agents — they run in Anthropic's cloud, not on the user's machine. They cannot access local files, local services, or local environment variables.
- Always convert cron to human-readable when displaying
- When listing routines, `ended_reason: "run_once_fired"` means a one-shot already ran (shows as "Ran" in the web UI). The user can re-arm it by updating with a new `run_once_at`.
- Default to `enabled: true` unless user says otherwise
- Accept GitHub URLs in any format (https://github.com/org/repo, org/repo, etc.) and normalize to the full HTTPS URL (without .git suffix)
- The prompt is the most important part — spend time getting it right. The cloud agent starts with zero context, so the prompt must be self-contained.
- To delete a routine, direct users to https://claude.ai/code/routines


## User Request

The user said: "Create a recurring cron job (every 20 minutes) for this repo (/Users/h4ng.l1u/Downloads/hackcamp27, gh/nougify/hackcamp27) that autonomously implements missing features overnight while the user is asleep and unreachable. I need guidance on the mechanics (does it run against this local checkout or a fresh clone? what context/instructions does each invocation get?) before I write the task prompt."

attachment.snippet:
1	# Mise
2	
3	Hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app: scan groceries, find real recipes that fit the pantry and diet, cook by gesture or voice, track nutrition. Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Auth0, Tiger Data (Postgres/TimescaleDB via postgres.js), Gemini, MediaPipe, ElevenLabs.
4	
5	@AGENTS.md
6	
7	Next 16 uses `src/proxy.ts`, not `middleware.ts`.
8	
9	Source of truth, highest first: `src/contracts/**`, then `SPEC.md`, then comments. If the contracts and SPEC disagree, the contracts win; raise the mismatch with a human. Workstream task lists: `jerry.md` (A, cook mode), `johnny.md` (B, pantry and nutrition), `hang.md` (C, recipes and cooking backend). Ownership by path: SPEC §3.2.
10	
11	## Commands
12	Node >= 22. Definition of done: typecheck, lint and test all pass.
13	
14	```bash
15	npm run dev
16	npm run typecheck   # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
17	npm run lint
18	npm test            # unit tests, no network or database; excludes *.db.test.ts
19	npm run test:db     # migrates DATABASE_URL_TEST, then runs *.db.test.ts
20	npm run migrate     # applies db/migrations/*.sql to DATABASE_URL
21	npm run build
22	```
23	
24	- Run one test file with `npx vitest run <path>`.
25	- `DATABASE_URL_TEST` must be a Tiger fork, never production.
26	- SPEC §14.1 lists `test:e2e`, but no such script exists yet.
27	- Local config lives in `.env.local` (template: `.env.example`). Never print its values.
28	- Without `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, non-production runs skip auth and act as a demo user (`src/lib/auth0.ts`).
29	
30	## Layout
31	- `src/app`: pages in `(app)/`, route handlers in `api/`.
32	- `src/server`: server-side domain logic by area (`pantry`, `products`, `vision`, `nutrition`, `recipes`, `diet`, `cook`).
33	- `src/features`: client components and hooks (`cook`, `gesture`, `voice`, `scan`, `pantry`, `nutrition`, `recipes`).
34	- `src/contracts`: shared domain and API types, plus fixtures.
35	- `src/lib`: env, db, auth, HTTP helpers, units, GTIN, rate limiting, Gemini client.
36	- `src/components/ui`: shared UI kit. Use it before adding new primitives.
37	
38	## Code conventions
39	- Route handlers follow `src/app/api/meals/route.ts`: `runtime = 'nodejs'`, `requireUser()` first inside `try`, Zod-validate input, respond with `jsonOk`/`jsonError`, and `catch (err) { return handleRouteError(err); }`. Check malformed path ids with `isUuid`.
40	- Rate-limit costly routes with `checkRateLimit(userId, route)` from `@/lib/rate-limit`.
41	- Database: `import sql from '@/lib/db'`. Types are parsed centrally: `numeric`/`int8` to number, `date` to a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string, `timestamptz` to `Date`.
42	- Every query on user data filters by `user_id`. Another user's id returns 404, not 403.
43	- `requireUser()` returns identity and `tz` only. Diets, allergens and onboarding state come from `src/server/pantry/profile.ts`.
44	- Read validated config with `getEnv()` from `@/lib/env`. Secrets never use `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
45	- Modules that touch the database, secrets or server-side APIs start with `import 'server-only'`.
46	- Fetch third-party recipe pages only through `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts` (SSRF protection).
47	- Unit tests sit next to the code as `*.test.ts`; tests that need a database are `*.db.test.ts`.
48	
49	## Product rules (SPEC §12, §13)
50	- Treat Gemini output as untrusted: validate it with Zod, verify ids, and re-check allergens in code.
51	- Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap. AI-generated or transformed content carries a visible badge; publisher content carries attribution.
52	- Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent. Colour is never the only signal.
53	- Camera frames and label or expiry photos are never stored.
54	
55	## Changing shared files (SPEC §18.5)
56	- `src/contracts/**`, `db/migrations/**`, `src/lib/**` and `src/components/ui/**` are frozen. Stop and ask a human. Changes go in one small additive commit titled `contract: …`.
57	- Add a new numbered migration (`000N_*.sql`) rather than editing an existing one.
58	- Do not edit `package.json` or the lockfile as part of feature work. Dependency changes go through the team's designated owner.
59	
60	# Team workflow (Entire + Claude Code)
61	
62	This repo uses Entire. Commits capture the Claude session as a checkpoint automatically. Run `entire agent-help` for exact CLI flags.
63	
64	## Branches and trails
65	- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
66	- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
67	- Keep features small; merge every few hours.
68	
69	## Before pushing
70	1. Run `entire review general` (local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail; the profile name is required when run non-interactively). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing. For a stacked branch, pass `--base <parent-branch>`.
71	2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
72	3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.
73	
74	## Finishing a feature
75	- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
76	- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.
77	
78	## Gotchas
79	- `entire review` is a labs command: `entire agent-help review` errors, so use `entire review --help` for its flags.
80	- `entire trail show` with no args returns 403; pass the number: `entire trail show <n> --project gh/nougify`.
81	- "project gh/nougify does not exist or is not visible" means the logged-in account lacks project access; a teammate has to grant it.
82	- In Git Bash, prefix `entire api` calls with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
83	- Ask the user before `entire enable/disable/clean/login` or granting project access.

1	# Johnny: §17 answers and decisions (Workstream B + auth/DB foundation)
2	
3	These answers are for a human to copy into SPEC.md §17. All five items (4, 5, 6, 7, 11) are resolved as of 2026-11-08.
4	
5	## §17 answers
6	
7	### 4. dataandapis.com: not-found shape, token cost, sodium unit, carbs, plan
8	**Verified 2026-11-08** (team key, 2 calls):
9	- **Miss:** HTTP **404**, `{"ok":false,"message":"Product '0000000000000' not found","tried":["0000000000000","00000000","000000000000","00000000000000"]}`. The API retries re-paddings itself.
10	- **Token cost:** the response header `ratelimit-requests-remaining` read **500 after the miss and 499 after the Nutella hit**, so a miss appears **not** to cost a token. Re-check on the dashboard if quota gets tight.
11	- **Plan:** a full allowance of 500 means the **Free plan** (500 tokens/month). The products cache and negative cache are essential.
12	- **Sodium:** `nutriments_per_100g.sodium` is **grams**. Nutella gives `0.043` against OFF's `0.0428 g`, and `salt` 0.107 ≈ sodium × 2.5. So `sodiumMg = sodium × 1000`.
13	- **Carbs:** `carbohydrates` 57.5 equals OFF's `carbohydrates_100g`, i.e. as printed. Team decision: store as printed (EU labels exclude fibre).
14	- **Fields seen:** `quantity` was `"400 g e"` (not null as the docs example showed), `serving_size` null, `allergens` `"Milk, Nuts, Soybeans"` (comma-separated English), `attribution {dataset, source:"Open Food Facts", source_url, licence:"ODbL v1.0"}`, `image_url`, `last_modified`, `completeness`.
15	- Latency was 389–718 ms. The Nutella body is saved as the adapter fixture.
16	
17	The adapter treats these as **miss**: any non-2xx other than 401/402/429/5xx, `ok:false`, or a missing `name`. Errors are never negatively cached.
18	
19	### 5. Open Food Facts v2 fields and not-found shape
20	**Verified 2026-11-07** (staging `world.openfoodfacts.net` plus one production read):
21	- **Found:** HTTP 200, `{"status":1,"status_verbose":"product found","product":{…}}`.
22	- **Valid but unknown GTIN:** **HTTP 404**, `{"code":"4821739056146","status":0,"status_verbose":"product not found"}`.
23	- **Invalid code** (e.g. all zeros): **HTTP 200**, `{"code":"00000000","status":0,"status_verbose":"no code or invalid code"}`. OFF strips leading zeros from the echoed code.
24	- So "`status !== 1` or HTTP 404 → miss" (§10.2) covers both cases.
25	- **Nutriment keys** (flat, v2):
26	  - Confirmed verbatim: `energy-kcal_100g`, `energy-kj_100g`, `proteins_100g`, `fat_100g`, `saturated-fat_100g`, `carbohydrates_100g`, `sugars_100g`, `fiber_100g` (US spelling), `sodium_100g`, `salt_100g`, plus `<name>_unit`.
27	  - `sodium_100g` is in **grams** (`sodium_unit: "g"`), so `sodiumMg = sodium_100g × 1000`.
28	  - `_serving` keys appear only when the product has serving data. Nutella currently has none.
29	- **Quantity:**
30	  - `product_quantity` is a number and `product_quantity_unit` a unit (Nutella: `400`, `"g"`).
31	  - `quantity` is free text (`"400 g e"`; the `e` is the EU estimated sign).
32	  - `serving_quantity` is in grams when present.
33	- **Staging data isn't realistic.** It holds test products for the GS1 example codes (`5901234123457` is "Pancakes"), and its Nutella has an empty `quantity`. Fixtures therefore come from a production read.
34	
35	### 6. Tiger: TimescaleDB present, hypertable syntax, tz-aware time_bucket, real-time cagg, connection string, storage cap
36	**Verified 2026-11-08** on `mise-test` (fork) and `mise-db`, both already migrated by a teammate with dev's `migrate.mjs`:
37	- **Extensions:** `timescaledb@2.31.0`, `timescaledb_toolkit@1.26.0`, `pgcrypto@1.4` on PostgreSQL 18.6. Session time zone is `Etc/UTC`.
38	- **Migrations:** `0001_init.sql` and `0002_timescale.sql` are in `schema_migrations` on both DBs. So **0002 runs fine inside a transaction** with dev's `migrate.mjs`; no no-transaction path is needed.
39	- **Hypertables:** `meal_logs` (`eaten_at`, 7-day chunks) and `pantry_events` (`occurred_at`, 7-day chunks). `WITH (tsdb.hypertable…)` accepted the composite PK `PRIMARY KEY (id, eaten_at)`.
40	- **Continuous aggregate:** `daily_nutrition` uses `time_bucket('1 day', eaten_at, 'America/Vancouver')`, so the tz argument works. `materialized_only = false` (real-time). The refresh policy runs every 15 min with start_offset 30 days and end_offset 1 hour.
41	- **Real-time check (§14.3 #4):** a meal inserted and read back in one rolled-back transaction showed up in `daily_nutrition` immediately (540 kcal / 32 g, 1 entry), served by the raw `meal_logs` part of the plan.
42	- **Tiger defaults not in our SQL:** `policy_compression` with `compress_after = 7 days` on both hypertables. TimescaleDB 2.31 supports UPDATE/DELETE on compressed chunks, so deleting an old meal still works.
43	- **Time zone:** both the DB tzdata and Node (tzdata 2026e) give America/Vancouver as **UTC−7 (PDT) on 2026-11-08**, i.e. BC's permanent Pacific time. Day buckets start 07:00 UTC, and Node's `local_date` and the cagg's `day` agree.
44	- **Connection string:** `postgres://tsdbadmin:<password>@<id>.<project>.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com:<port>/tsdb?sslmode=require`. **The password must be added by hand**, because the Tiger CLI/console string omits it. Special characters need URL-encoding.
45	- **Storage cap:** not checked (the 750 MB figure is still third-party). Both DBs are empty.
46	- Migration 0003 (grace days, `johnny/contract-grace`) is **not applied yet**. Apply it after that branch merges: `npm run migrate -- --test`, then `npm run migrate`.
47	
48	### 7. `auth0.getSession()` with no args in route handlers
49	**Partly verified 2026-11-08** against the real tenant (`next dev`, no browser):
50	- Signed-out `GET /api/pantry` returns **401** `{"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"No active session"}}`. So the no-arg `getSession()` runs inside a route handler and returns null without a session.
51	- Signed-out `GET /today` returns **307 → /auth/login**.
52	- `/auth/login` returns **307 → https://nougify.ca.auth0.com/authorize** (PKCE S256, scope `openid profile email offline_access`, `redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback`).
53	- **Browser login (F1 AC2), verified 2026-11-08:** Google sign-in → sign-out → sign-in again against `mise-db`. Exactly **one** `users` row was created for the account (`auth0_sub` `google-oauth2|…`, email and name filled in, `tz` America/Vancouver, `onboarded_at` null). `last_seen_at` moved on the second login, and there are no duplicate `sub`s. So the session-backed `getSession()` and `requireUser()` upsert work in a real request.
54	- `mise-db` also holds a second user, created earlier by another Google account (a teammate testing). Expected: the dev server writes to the shared `DATABASE_URL`.
55	
56	How sign-in is enforced on `dev`:
57	- `src/proxy.ts` only runs `auth0.middleware()`, which mounts `/auth/*` and rolls sessions. It's skipped when `authDisabled`, i.e. outside production with no `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, where everyone is a demo user.
58	- `requireUser()` throws `UnauthorizedError`. Route handlers turn it into a 401 `ApiError` JSON via `handleRouteError`, and `(app)/layout.tsx` turns it into a redirect to `/auth/login`.
59	- This covers F1 AC1 as long as every route handler uses `try { … } catch (err) { return handleRouteError(err) }`.
60	
61	### 11. Allergen enum vs Health Canada priority allergens
62	Health Canada's priority allergens are peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, milk, eggs, fish, crustaceans, molluscs, soy, wheat and triticale, and mustard, plus sulphites and gluten sources (barley, oats, rye).
63	
64	Decision (team): **keep the `Allergen` enum unchanged** and document the mapping:
65	- `shellfish` = crustaceans **and** molluscs
66	- `wheat_gluten` = wheat, triticale, barley, oats, rye (gluten sources)
67	- The other values map one-to-one.
68	
69	## Other decisions
70	- **Env validation:** dev's `getEnv()` parses only partially during `next build` and in tests, warns in local dev, and throws in production. `src/instrumentation.ts` calls it at server start, so production fails at boot with the missing variable names.
71	  - Verified: `next build` passes with no `.env.local`.
72	  - Verified: `next start` in production with no env logs the names and "Failed to prepare server".
73	  - Caveat: in that failed state the `next start` process stayed alive instead of exiting.
74	- **DB types (`src/lib/db.ts`):** `numeric` and `int8` are parsed to JS numbers. `date` stays a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string. `timestamptz` comes back as a `Date`. Existing callers already wrap values in `Number()` and accept `string | Date` dates.
75	- **`.env.example`:** dev's file (whitelisted in `.gitignore`).
76	- **GTIN (`src/lib/gtin.ts`):**
77	  - Spaces, hyphens and dots are stripped; letters give `non_numeric`.
78	  - UPC-E expands to GTIN-13. Scanner `upc_e` is always expanded; a typed 8-digit code is tried as EAN-8 first.
79	  - A GTIN-14 with indicator 0 collapses to GTIN-13. This changed one expectation in dev's `gtin.test.ts`.
80	  - `normalizeGtin(raw, format?)` keeps dev's `{ ok, gtin }` shape. `normalizeBarcode()` also returns `lookupCode` and `kind`.
81	  - EAN-8 uses its 8 digits for provider calls and the 13-digit padded form as the key.
82	- **Label basis:** Gemini's `per_serving` maps to `ProductDraft.basis = 'serving'`. F3 AC1's `'per_serving'` wording is the schema value, not the contract value.
83	- **Normalizer:** `normalized_name` comes from `src/server/pantry/normalize.ts` (Johnny). Hang's recipe ingredient parser imports it, so matching uses identical rules.
84	
85	## Products and vision notes (johnny/products, 2026-11-08)
86	
87	- Live check on the test fork: Nutella cold 1.2 s, warm 18 ms; bad check digit never reaches a provider; a garbage dataandapis key falls through to OFF and writes `error/401`.
88	- A date with no printed year resolves to its next occurrence **on or after** today. SPEC says "after today"; a package stamped with today's date means today.
89	- When a stale product can't be refreshed (providers failed or missed), the old row is served rather than `not_found`.
90	- Per-serving labels stay `basis: 'serving'` in the API. The client converts to per-100 when it fills the form, and drops the numbers if no serving weight was read.
91	- `proxy.ts` makes Next buffer at most 10 MB of a body, so the vision routes answer 413 above 10 MB total even though 3 x 4 MB is 12 MB. Client downscaling keeps real uploads far below that. `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize` in next.config.ts would lift it.
92	- Gemini label and expiry reading is tested with mocks only: the Gemini API was down during this work. Run F3 AC1-3 and F4 AC3-5 on real photos once it is back.
93	
94	## Nutrition notes (johnny/nutrition, 2026-11-08)
95	
96	- Team decisions: an item or product with no calorie data can't be logged (missing protein alone counts as 0); deleting a meal never changes the pantry; the 7-day chart shows calories with a goal line, protein in the tooltip and table.
97	- A pantry deduction larger than the stock is clamped to the stock, matching finish-cooking. The meal still records what was eaten.
98	- `DELETE /api/meals/:id` matches `eaten_at` within its millisecond: rows from the database's `now()` have microseconds and JS dates don't.
99	- A meal back-dated into an already-materialized day reaches the 7-day chart only after the next aggregate refresh (15 minutes at most). The UI only logs meals at the current time, and "today" comes from the real-time part of the aggregate.
100	- History days are bucketed in America/Vancouver (migration 0002). For users elsewhere the rings (their local day) and chart can differ near midnight; SPEC §5.3 accepts this.

- **Extensions:** `timescaledb@2.31.0`, `timescaledb_toolkit@1.26.0`, `pgcrypto@1.4` on PostgreSQL 18.6. Session time zone is `Etc/UTC`.
- **Migrations:** `0001_init.sql` and `0002_timescale.sql` are in `schema_migrations` on both DBs. So **0002 runs fine inside a transaction** with dev's `migrate.mjs`; no no-transaction path is needed.
- **Hypertables:** `meal_logs` (`eaten_at`, 7-day chunks) and `pantry_events` (`occurred_at`, 7-day chunks). `WITH (tsdb.hypertable…)` accepted the composite PK `PRIMARY KEY (id, eaten_at)`.
- **Continuous aggregate:** `daily_nutrition` uses `time_bucket('1 day', eaten_at, 'America/Vancouver')`, so the tz argument works. `materialized_only = false` (real-time). The refresh policy runs every 15 min with start_offset 30 days and end_offset 1 hour.
- **Real-time check (§14.3 #4):** a meal inserted and read back in one rolled-back transaction showed up in `daily_nutrition` immediately (540 kcal / 32 g, 1 entry), served by the raw `meal_logs` part of the plan.

- **Time zone:** both the DB tzdata and Node (tzdata 2026e) give America/Vancouver as **UTC−7 (PDT) on 2026-11-08**, i.e. BC's permanent Pacific time. Day buckets start 07:00 UTC, and Node's `local_date` and the cagg's `day` agree.
- **Connection string:** `postgres://tsdbadmin:<password>@<id>.<project>.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com:<port>/tsdb?sslmode=require`. **The password must be added by hand**, because the Tiger CLI/console string omits it. Special characters need URL-encoding.
- **Storage cap:** not checked (the 750 MB figure is still third-party). Both DBs are empty.
- Migration 0003 (grace days, `johnny/contract-grace`) is **not applied yet**. Apply it after that branch merges: `npm run migrate -- --test`, then `npm run migrate`.

### 7. `auth0.getSession()` with no args in route handlers
**Partly verified 2026-11-08** against the real tenant (`next dev`, no browser):
- Signed-out `GET /api/pantry` returns **401** `{"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"No active session"}}`. So the no-arg `getSession()` runs inside a route handler and returns null without a session.
- Signed-out `GET /today` returns **307 → /auth/login**.
- `/auth/login` returns **307 → https://nougify.ca.auth0.com/authorize** (PKCE S256, scope `openid profile email offline_access`, `redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback`).
- **Browser login (F1 AC2), verified 2026-11-08:** Google sign-in → sign-out → sign-in again against `mise-db`. Exactly **one** `users` row was created for the account (`auth0_sub` `google-oauth2|…`, email and name filled in, `tz` America/Vancouver, `onboarded_at` null). `last_seen_at` moved on the second login, and there are no duplicate `sub`s. So the session-backed `getSession()` and `requireUser()` upsert work in a real request.
- `mise-db` also holds a second user, created earlier by another Google account (a teammate testing). Expected: the dev server writes to the shared `DATABASE_URL`.

- `src/proxy.ts` only runs `auth0.middleware()`, which mounts `/auth/*` and rolls sessions. It's skipped when `authDisabled`, i.e. outside production with no `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, where everyone is a demo user.
- `requireUser()` throws `UnauthorizedError`. Route handlers turn it into a 401 `ApiError` JSON via `handleRouteError`, and `(app)/layout.tsx` turns it into a redirect to `/auth/login`.
- This covers F1 AC1 as long as every route handler uses `try { … } catch (err) { return handleRouteError(err) }`.

### 11. Allergen enum vs Health Canada priority allergens
Health Canada's priority allergens are peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, milk, eggs, fish, crustaceans, molluscs, soy, wheat and triticale, and mustard, plus sulphites and gluten sources (barley, oats, rye).

Decision (team): **keep the `Allergen` enum unchanged** and document the mapping:
- `shellfish` = crustaceans **and** molluscs
- `wheat_gluten` = wheat, triticale, barley, oats, rye (gluten sources)

  - Verified: `next start` in production with no env logs the names and "Failed to prepare server".
  - Caveat: in that failed state the `next start` process stayed alive instead of exiting.
- **DB types (`src/lib/db.ts`):** `numeric` and `int8` are parsed to JS numbers. `date` stays a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string. `timestamptz` comes back as a `Date`. Existing callers already wrap values in `Number()` and accept `string | Date` dates.
- **`.env.example`:** dev's file (whitelisted in `.gitignore`).
- **GTIN (`src/lib/gtin.ts`):**
  - Spaces, hyphens and dots are stripped; letters give `non_numeric`.
  - UPC-E expands to GTIN-13. Scanner `upc_e` is always expanded; a typed 8-digit code is tried as EAN-8 first.
  - A GTIN-14 with indicator 0 collapses to GTIN-13. This changed one expectation in dev's `gtin.test.ts`.
  - `normalizeGtin(raw, format?)` keeps dev's `{ ok, gtin }` shape. `normalizeBarcode()` also returns `lookupCode` and `kind`.
  - EAN-8 uses its 8 digits for provider calls and the 13-digit padded form as the key.
- **Label basis:** Gemini's `per_serving` maps to `ProductDraft.basis = 'serving'`. F3 AC1's `'per_serving'` wording is the schema value, not the contract value.

- Live check on the test fork: Nutella cold 1.2 s, warm 18 ms; bad check digit never reaches a provider; a garbage dataandapis key falls through to OFF and writes `error/401`.

- Gemini label and expiry reading is tested with mocks only: the Gemini API was down during this work. Run F3 AC1-3 and F4 AC3-5 on real photos once it is back.

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
   If it doesn't need another iteration, stop instead (step 6) — re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then make the same decision. If the loop should continue, call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 (the Monitor remains the wake signal; the new wakeup is only the fallback heartbeat). If the event means the work is finished, stop (step 6).
6. **To stop the loop** — the task is complete, further iterations can't make progress, or the user asked you to stop — call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` (no other fields) and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Stopping is the loop's normal ending — the user can restart it anytime with /loop.

1	import 'server-only';
2	import postgres from 'postgres';
3	import { getEnv } from './env';
4	
5	const env = getEnv();
6	
7	/**
8	 * One small pool per long-lived Node process (SPEC.md §3.1) — Tiger's free
9	 * tier excludes connection pooling, and postgres.js connects lazily on first
10	 * query, so constructing this at module load does not open a connection.
11	 *
12	 * `MISE_TEST_DB=1` (set by `npm run test:db`) points at DATABASE_URL_TEST,
13	 * a Tiger fork — never production.
14	 */
15	const url =
16	  process.env.MISE_TEST_DB === '1' ? (env.DATABASE_URL_TEST ?? '') : (env.DATABASE_URL ?? '');
17	
18	/**
19	 * Type parsing (shared by every workstream):
20	 *   numeric (1700), int8 (20) → JS number (contracts use `number`; our values fit in 2^53)
21	 *   date (1082)               → 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, never a Date (a Date would shift by the TZ)
22	 *   timestamptz               → Date (postgres.js default); call .toISOString() for contracts
23	 * Serializers match postgres.js defaults: numbers/strings as text; a Date for a `date` column is
24	 * written as its UTC day, as postgres.js v4 does. Callers may still wrap values in Number().
25	 */
26	const asText = (x: unknown) => String(x);
27	const toNumber = (x: string) => Number(x);
28	
29	const sql = postgres(url, {
30	  max: env.DB_POOL_MAX ?? 5,
31	  ssl: 'require',
32	  types: {
33	    numericAsNumber: { to: 1700, from: [1700], serialize: asText, parse: toNumber },
34	    int8AsNumber: { to: 20, from: [20], serialize: asText, parse: toNumber },
35	    dateAsIsoString: {
36	      to: 1082,
37	      from: [1082],
38	      serialize: (x: unknown) => (x instanceof Date ? x.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : String(x)),
39	      parse: (x: string) => x,
40	    },
41	  },
42	});

Diagnosed it with `curl` directly (bypassing the browser): `/today` and `/api/health` both return a bare 500 with an **empty body** — no JSON error page, nothing. The landing page (`/`) still works fine (200) on both domains. That pattern — static pages work, anything touching `src/lib/db.ts` 500s instantly — matches one specific cause: `db.ts` calls `getEnv()` at **module load time**, and in production `getEnv()` throws synchronously if any required env var is missing.

Checking `main`'s current `env.ts`, the Vertex AI migration (merged a while back) made `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` a hard-required field with no default. content.text:
**Status update — this is a real one:** found and fixed a genuine integration bug between the two workstreams. Johnny's `pastBestBeforeGraceDays` setting (grace period past the best-before date) was already wired into the "expiring soon" list and pantry colouring, but its own doc comment names a third place it should apply — **recipe matching** — which never got it. `pantryForMatching` hard-excluded anything past its date regardless of the user's grace setting, and `getProfileFilters` didn't even fetch the column. So a user who set, say, a 3-day grace period would still never get recipes suggested for items in that grace window.

Fixed across all 6 real call sites (recipe search, recipe detail, adapt, finish-preview, finish-transaction) plus added the first unit tests for `pantryForMatching` (previously zero coverage). All backward-compatible (`graceDays` defaults to `0`). 625/625 tests pass, typecheck/lint/build clean. Pushed as another fixup commit onto `integrate-johnny` (now at `f24b15c`) — still not merged, still waiting on your `entire review general` approval.

Since you're up now — want me to keep running the 20-min loop, or pause it while we sort out the production 500 error?

content.text:
On the server:

```bash
cd ~/hackcamp27
echo "GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<your-gcp-project-id>" >> .env.production
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web
```

You'll need the actual GCP project id — whoever set up Vertex AI for the `jerry/vertex-ai` branch (check `gcp-sa.json`'s `project_id` field on the server, or ask Jerry) will have it. Also worth checking `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is actually mounted correctly (`docker-compose.yml` expects `./gcp-sa.json` to exist in `~/hackcamp27` on the server) — if that file's missing too, Vertex AI calls will fail even after this fix, just with a different error at call time rather than at boot.

attachment.prompt: no but i want to log in for prod, would logging in on this mac allow prod to work

content.text:
No — logging into `gcloud` on this Mac doesn't make prod work by itself. Here's the actual chain:

- **Production auth** (the Vultr server) uses a **service-account key file** (`gcp-sa.json`), not a personal login. `docker-compose.yml` mounts that file into the container (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS: /run/secrets/gcp-sa.json`). A server process can't do an interactive browser OAuth login, which is why it needs this file instead.
- **`gcloud auth login` on this Mac** only lets *this Mac's* `gcloud` CLI act as you, so you can run the `gcloud iam service-accounts create/add-iam-policy-binding/keys create` commands you pasted earlier — those commands are what *generates* `gcp-sa.json` in the first place.
- After that, you still have to `scp` the generated `gcp-sa.json` to the Vultr server, make sure `.env.production` has `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`/`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, and restart the container. That's the step that actually makes prod work.

So: this Mac's gcloud login is just step 1 of 4 — the key-minting step, done locally, by whichever Google account has IAM rights on the project (probably whoever set up `jerry/vertex-ai` — if that's not you, you'll need them to either grant you access or run the service-account creation themselves).

Want to proceed with `gcloud auth login` now to check whether your Google account actually has access to that GCP project?

Found it — look closely at what you pasted:

```
DATABASE_URL= postgres://tsdbadmin@vtb7pcud9m.gq06qz0iv4.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com:30107/tsdb?sslmode=require
```

**There's no password in that connection string at all** — it's `tsdbadmin@host`, not `tsdbadmin:<password>@host`. My redaction `sed` only matches `user:password@`, and it printed the URL completely unchanged, which means the regex found no `:password@` to redact — there genuinely isn't one there.

This matches a gotcha already documented in this repo's own `docs/johnny-verify.md`: *"The password must be added by hand, because the Tiger CLI/console string omits it."* Whoever set up `.env.production` pasted the connection string straight from the Tiger console, which deliberately omits the password, and nobody added it back in. That's almost certainly why `db: down` — Postgres is rejecting the connection outright.

**Fix:** edit `.env.production` on the server and insert the actual Tiger DB password between `tsdbadmin` and `@`:

```
DATABASE_URL=postgres://tsdbadmin:<the-real-password>@vtb7pcud9m.gq06qz0iv4.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com:30107/tsdb?sslmode=require
```

You'll need that password from wherever Tiger credentials are stored for the team (password manager / whoever provisioned `mise-db`). Also worth double-checking there's no stray leading space after `DATABASE_URL=` in the actual file (hard to tell from a terminal paste) — `cat -A .env.production | grep DATABASE_URL` would show it plainly if so.

message.content: but why when I click sign in in were.cooking, it goes directly to https://now.were.cooking/today

content.text:
That's expected behavior, not a bug — it's SSO (single sign-on) working as designed. Here's the actual chain:

1. Click "Sign in" on `were.cooking` → request goes to `/auth/login?returnTo=/today`.
2. Caddy's `were.cooking` block doesn't serve that path directly (only `/`, `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico` are served locally) — it redirects to `https://now.were.cooking/auth/login?returnTo=/today`.
3. `now.were.cooking`'s Caddy block only intercepts the exact path `/` (for the logged-out-redirect and `/today` shortcuts) — `/auth/login` doesn't match either rule, so it passes straight through to the Next.js app.
4. The Auth0 SDK sends you to Auth0's `/authorize` endpoint. **If your browser already has an active session with Auth0 (or with Google, if you signed in via Google) from earlier testing**, Auth0 recognizes that and completes the login silently — no login form shown — then redirects straight back to `/auth/callback` and on to `/today` (per the `returnTo`).

So you're not skipping login, you're just already logged in at the identity-provider level, and OAuth SSO correctly doesn't make you re-enter credentials for a session that's still valid. If you want to see the real login screen again (e.g. to test a fresh user's flow), open a private/incognito window, or actually sign out first (which should go through `/auth/logout`).

But heads up — you have 3-4 of these branches, and they're **all based on that same `main` tip**, not stacked on each other. So:

```bash
git push origin hang-nav-logout:main   # ✅ works, fast-forward
git push origin hang-landing-polish:main   # ❌ rejected (non-fast-forward) — this branch doesn't have nav-logout's commit
```

That second push will just get safely rejected (git won't let you accidentally lose the first commit), not break anything. To merge all of them this way, after each successful push you'd need to update the next branch first:

```bash
git push origin hang-nav-logout:main
git switch hang-landing-polish && git rebase main && git push origin hang-landing-polish:main
git switch hang-status-dashboard && git rebase main && git push origin hang-status-dashboard:main
```

1	# Team workflow (Entire + Claude Code)
2	
3	This repo uses Entire. Commits capture the Claude session as a checkpoint automatically. Run `entire agent-help` for exact CLI flags.
4	
5	## Branches and trails
6	- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
7	- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
8	- Keep features small; merge every few hours.
9	
10	## Before pushing
11	1. Run `entire review` (profile `general`: local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing.
12	2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
13	3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.
14	
15	## Finishing a feature
16	- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
17	- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.
18	
19	## Gotchas
20	- `entire trail show` with no args returns 403; pass the number: `entire trail show <n> --project gh/nougify`.
21	- In Git Bash, prefix `entire api` calls with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
22	- Ask the user before `entire enable/disable/clean/login` or granting project access.

I checked exhaustively — every commit author field *and* every `Co-authored-by:` trailer, across all 19 branches and every tag fetched from origin. Nothing matches HarukaMa's account anywhere. The only co-authors appearing are `noreply@anthropic.com` (from Claude Code checkpoint commits — looks like at least two different sessions/models touched this repo, "Claude Opus 5.5" and "Claude Sonnet 5").

So this isn't a real entry in the repo's current history — there's no commit for me to fix. Most likely explanation: GitHub's Contributors graph/Insights page is a cached, eventually-consistent computation, and it's showing a stale attribution from some earlier state (e.g. a commit that existed briefly with a wrong email before being amended or rebased away during all the rapid-fire pushing tonight). HarukaMa's bio itself ("If you see my name in your commit...") confirms this happens to them across many unrelated repos — it's a known GitHub quirk, not something specific to something we did wrong just now.

There's nothing to git-fix here. If it's bothering you, the usual remedies are: wait for GitHub to recompute (can take a while), or push a new commit to main to nudge a recompute — but I wouldn't expect either to be guaranteed. Want me to leave it alone, or is there a specific repo setting (like Settings → Collaborators) you want me to check instead?
